title: an unlocked reference-count decrement drifts below the true number of holders
live_proof: the fix is in the pinned tree: process_mget_cmd's error path calls do_item_remove only when of.locked, and item_remove -- which takes the lock -- otherwise. The case reconstructs the pre-fix path, which called do_item_remove either way
object: an item, i.e. one chunk of a slab class, held by two clients at once
lifetime_ender: do_item_remove (items.c:538) when the drifted count reaches zero: item_free -> slabs_free, and the chunk goes on its class's slots list, never to free()
shape: unlocked refcount update / count drifts below the holders / slabs reuse / read through the dead pointer
allocator_layer: slabs.c size classes over 1 MiB pages, memcached 1.6.45
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: slabs.c is upstream's file at the 1.6.45 pin and makes every allocation decision. The item layer is reduced to item_free and do_item_remove; the lost update is written out as the three steps of refcount_decr (memcached.h:1041) with the concurrent get landing between them, because that interleaving IS the defect and a single -- would hide it
distinguishing: the count here is neither overwritten (case 2) nor overflowed (case 3): it is simply one short of the truth, and nothing in the allocator or the item layer can tell. The free that follows looks correct at every step

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES. exit=0, completed=1, object_reuses=0, chunk_reuses=1. Not caught. The reuse counters are the point: the storage really was handed back out, which is the situation revocation would have to catch if the memory reached free(). It does not -- cache.c keeps it on its own STAILQ and slabs.c returns it to the page, so libc's quarantine never holds it. EVIDENCE COMMITTED 2026-10-06: results/20261006-cheribsd/. Both controls are in that bundle -- the revocation control FAULTED with addr == pc == the independently resolved expectation (0x101e42), proving the revoker sweeps in this guest AND attributing the fault; and a NEGATIVE CONTROL run on the same vehicle makes all 8 case oracles FAIL while the three platform controls still pass, so none of these completions is vacuous. The image hash is byte-identical to the vehicle the ffmpeg readings of the same day used, so the two programs' columns are comparable.
cheribsd-revocation.control: the control fired in the SAME boot: revocation-control exit=162 signal=34 (SIGPROT) si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) with pc == the address the supervisor resolved independently (0x101e42). The platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds passed in the same run.

NOT the PoisonCap platform the 2026-09-21 bundles used, so those hashes differ by construction.

native-detect.requires: the chunk never reaches free(), so ASan has no event; it would see the reuse only as an ordinary live object
native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g; port library with the same sanitizer). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 67108864` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 67108864` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (3ef5169ae90b); the arm was previously 'not written'.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-stock-malloc/run-asan.txt: SILENT -- the defect reproduced (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED) and ASan printed nothing; built with MCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON (each page and cache.c object its own malloc, as upstream); both controls reported in the same run

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm loses the concurrent get inside the unlocked decrement, so the next release frees an item still held and the next slabs_alloc returns the same chunk; the fixed arm serialises the two and the count never reaches zero
native-fix-differential.note: unit_reissued differs between the arms, as in cases 2 and 3

sublet-malloc.target: Capstone domain, the allocators port's ledger in mode 2: stock slabs.c/cache.c on Sublet as the SYSTEM allocator -- a chunk carries its whole page's bound, an object its own, and nothing is revoked until a page or object is given back
sublet-malloc.oracle: the sequence completes: the lost decrement frees the chunk into its class's free list, not to free() MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-sublet-malloc/: the sequence COMPLETES, NOT CAUGHT (completed=1, image d714de5b223834bf).

note: the upstream message calls the effect 'refcount drift on a busy item' leading to 'memory corruption', and says it is inert unless someone is constantly sending overlarge opaques; this records the corruption step, not its likelihood
nested_why: memcached's slab allocator carved the object out of a 1 MiB page it owns -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NESTED.
